연구 방법: [초록 원문] Early observations on the effectiveness of the Compulsory Dog Microchipping policy, which was introduced across Great Britain in 2016, indicated improved reunification of stray dogs with their owners and an overall reduction in stray dogs handled by UK Local Authorities.

저자: Riti Thummalapenta
제목: Financial Sustainability in Animal Shelters: Insights from Public Records, Interviews, and Existing Research
연구 목적: [초록 원문] Animal shelters are organizations that take care of stray, abandoned, or surrendered animals, primarily cats and dogs, through temporary housing, medical treatment, and the facilitation of their adoption.These organizations serve to benefit both the animals and members of the local community by caring for animals that have nowhere else to go.In addition, they help to prevent the spread of disease and other community problems caused by stray animals.Despite these benefits, shelters often face instability and risk being shut down.This paper asks: What strategies help animal shelters remain financially sustainable while improving animal welfare outcomes?Answering this question is important because shelters provide essential services to both animals and communities, yet many struggle to stay financially sustainable while maintaining strong welfare outcomes.This study utilized a mixed-methods approach that combined a focused literature review, analysis of publicly available shelter data and financial documents from the Dallas-Fort Worth region, and interviews with representatives from both a municipal shelter and a nonprofit shelter.These methods were specifically chosen in order to compare existing research with real operational and financial patterns as well as on-the-job professional insights.At the conclusion of this study, it was clear that animal shelter sustainability must include not only funding but also positive animal outcomes, such as reducing euthanasia, increasing live-release rates, and maintaining humane care standards.It was evident that this is best achieved through the combination of several factors including stabilized and diversified funding, active length-of-stay (LOS) management, foster and volunteer capacity, and adoption practices suited to the shelter's intake structure.
학술지: The Oxford Journal of Student Scholarship
